answer.evidence: The platform band at rows 2-17 shows planks and sandbags seen from above. It ends in a light front-edge line at row 17 (#d6b073) with a dark shadow row at 18 (#192737). The tarp at the top right is a sloped diagonal-striped plane (rows 0-12). Below, the sheet-metal skirt (rows 19-25) and the braced legs with ladder and footings (rows 26-63) form a front face of 45 rows. The plank landing at rows 41-47 has a light front edge, so it also reads as a horizontal surface. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, narrow tower, about 1.5 tiles wide, set against two large house references. Its measured facts are healthy: 14 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted (dark brown beside wood) and not a black sticker line. The ramps are shallower than the references. Planks, the tarp and the sandbag rim show about 3-4 steps each, where the references show 5-6 per material on roof tiles and plaster speckle. The tower is a thin, sparse object with little grain on the legs, skirt and footings, so by eye it reads thinner and simpler than the references, with less per-element highlighting. The 14 tones come mostly from many small differently-coloured parts, not from deep ramps within a material. A careful artist would likely see it as a bit flatter than Beodeul next to the references, and when in doubt this fails.

answer.evidence: The platform is a plank deck seen from above, rows 2-17. Its sandbag rows and plank rows are foreshortened, and a light front-edge line at row 17 is followed by a dark shadow line at row 18. The tarp corner at the top right is a sloped roof plane above its own edge. Below the deck is a 7-row sheet-metal skirt (rows 19-25) and then an open leg section with ladder and braces (rows 28-63), which gives a front face well over 3 rows. The plank landing at rows 41-47 also has a top band ending in a lighter edge line at row 46. The overall structure shows top surfaces plus a front face, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 14 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 12 and 10 for the references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references. None of its dark edge pixels are neutral (0%), so the outline is a tinted dark brown beside the planks and tarp, not a sticker line. The planks, sandbag rim, tarp, metal skirt, braced legs and ladder are separated by value with plank grain and speckle, and no large area is a single flat colour. It is a small piece with only about 33 distinct colours in total, and each material ramp shows roughly 4 steps against the references' 5-6, so it is slightly shallower in shading. That is not enough to look thinner or flatter than the references, because the tile-level tone count is at or above theirs.
